gaps.sentence: The lecture was dull; ___, the students stayed awake out of politeness.
I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: She earns a very good salary; ___, she never seems to have any money.
gaps.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts two facts, like but, in a slightly more formal way.

gaps.sentence: I'll take the job ___ they don't offer me any more money.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a future possibility that will not change the decision.

gaps.sentence: ___ his impressive qualifications, he wasn't even shortlisted.
She took notes during the seminar ___ she could write it up that evening.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of the action.

gaps.sentence: The prototype is undeniably elegant; it is, ___, hopelessly impractical.
gaps.explanation: 'On the other hand' concedes elegance while introducing the drawback.

gaps.sentence: ___ being the youngest competitor, she won the gold medal.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite being...' is the standard concessive pattern with a gerund.
